sections.overview: The Slaty Skimmer is a North American dragonfly found mainly in the eastern United States and adjacent southeastern Canada.
sections.identification: Mature males have a slate-blue body and dark face, while females and immature males are brown with a dark dorsal stripe. Each wing has a dark spot near its outer leading edge. It resembles the Bar-winged Skimmer (L. axilena), but dark wing bars distinguish that species; see its profile.
sections.habitat: It frequents ponds and other still waters, often near woodland; some regional accounts also record it along slow streams.
sections.diet: Adults catch flying insects; the sources consulted do not quantify its prey or describe the larval diet in detail.
sections.behavior: Males perch at the water’s edge and defend small territories; females lay eggs in water or on aquatic plants while males may guard them.
sections.reproduction: Females deposit eggs in or over water, often onto aquatic vegetation; the references reviewed do not establish one larval development time across the range.
sections.ecology: Among the three Libellula described here, its eastern range contrasts with western L. forensis; L. luctuosa extends farther across North America.
sections.conservation: The Illinois account describes the species as common locally; that regional observation does not establish a global population trend.
